analysis.title: Multi-Asset Strategy Daily
key_insights: USTs are still struggling to find relief after last week's hawkish repricing. Friday ended with another bear-steepening move: 10Y UST yields tested 5.17% and 30s briefly approached 5.50%, while the front end held up better as a renewed tech sell-off gave it some support.

Fed speak should do most of the work today, with little on the data calendar. Warsh speaks from 5pm London, alongside Barr, Williams and Daly. After last week's CPI pushed December pricing toward another hike (27bp priced), Mizuho sees a high hurdle for a material further sell-off from Fed rhetoric alone.
Tomorrow's retail sales and Wednesday's FOMC minutes matter more for whether the market can validate the amount of 2027 tightening now priced.

Middle East risk is the other complication. Iran launched fresh drone attacks on a US facility in Bahrain over the weekend, Saudi-backed Yemeni forces pulled back from the Bab al-Mandeb area, and Iran claimed tankers struck mines around Hormuz. Brent is around the Friday highs in the mid-$90s.
USD rates face an awkward mix: weaker risk sentiment with S&P futures under pressure can support duration, while upside oil risks argue against chasing a duration bid.

Bunds opened with a small bid after Friday's long-end-led sell-off. Mizuho sees a high hurdle for ECB speakers to add materially to tightening expectations, but elevated underlying inflation, Brent in the mid-$90s and a EUR30bn-plus EGB supply week limit room for a duration rally.
France is worth watching after weekend protests and ahead of OAT supply later this week. S&P affirmed Italy at BBB+ on Friday. EUR/USD is under pressure around 1.1020.

UK jobs data tomorrow and CPI on Wednesday will show whether the hawkish BoE repricing has further to run. Greene argued for proactive action on inflation and Pill left the door open to tightening beyond December.

The BoE faces a tension: labour-market slack has not pushed wage growth significantly lower. Sticky wages plus a firm services CPI would support current BoE hiking pricing into 2027, while pay growth catching down would make the repricing hard to extend.

10Y Gilt yields closed Friday around 5.34% with the long end leading the sell-off. Mizuho would be reluctant to fade the move aggressively ahead of the data despite softer Rightmove numbers. GBP/USD is near 1.32.

Asian equities opened the week with better risk sentiment, then fell ahead of key tech earnings this week and on softer Chinese and Japanese activity data. JGBs twist-steepened and USD/JPY fell below 159.50 after testing 160 last week. DXY is near the recent high of 103.4.
earnings_insights: Key tech earnings are due this week and weighed on Asian equities. No figures are given.
